purpose: First authorized unblinding of H1-H3 for prospective held-out and cross-jurisdiction generalizability evaluation.
snapshot_policy: Repository artifacts freeze normalized semantic requirements and source/version/access metadata. Source-document bytes are not redistributed; later semantic changes are post-test amendments.

sources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov / AACT
sources.jurisdiction_scope: international registry with U.S. federal hosting
sources.version_or_release: ClinicalTrials.gov API 2.0.5; dataTimestamp 2026-08-10T09:00:05; AACT live schema accessed 2026-08-20
sources.evidence_basis: ClinicalTrials.gov API/study structure plus AACT relational schema conventions and table relationships.
sources.held_out_use_boundary: Semantic structure only for E8 first-pass generalizability; no H1-driven ontology adaptation before first-pass results are preserved.

sources.name: openFDA Drug Shortages
sources.version_or_release: official download page reported one file last updated 2026-07-23; API documentation accessed 2026-08-20
sources.evidence_basis: Native shortage fields plus openFDA harmonized drug identifiers.
sources.held_out_use_boundary: First-pass shortage representation/generalizability only; source-record fields are not automatically promoted to ontology classes.

sources.name: India National List of Essential Medicines 2022
sources.version_or_release: NLEM 2022, released 2022-09-13; official PDF 157 pages; accessed 2026-08-20
sources.evidence_basis: Medicine entries stratified by therapeutic section and Primary/Secondary/Tertiary level, with dosage-form and strength semantics.
sources.held_out_use_boundary: National EML cross-jurisdiction sample only; one national list is not treated as proof of global essential-medicine generalizability.
